questions.prompt: In the backtest loop, why does the fill happen before the books are marked at the close?
options: Because marking first would make the signal wrong
Because the fill changes the shares, and the close must value the shares you hold after it
Because fills can only happen at the close
Because marking to market is skipped on days with a fill
questions.explanation: The order trades at the open, so by the close you hold the new shares. Marking after the fill values those shares, as on 2025-03-07: 48 × 107 = 5136 in holdings.

questions.prompt: After the close of 107, equity is 10,120 and the signal is unchanged. Without the rule that resizes only on a signal change, what would the loop do?
options: Nothing, because the signal is still +1
Sell 1 share, because 0.5 × 10,120 / 107 rounds down to 47
questions.explanation: The target would be 0.5 × 10,120 / 107 = 47.29, so 47 shares against 48 held. The loop would trade 1 share for no reason, and would do so again whenever equity moves.

questions.prompt: On the same 500 bars, the loop returns −9.54% and the vectorised backtest −8.32%. What explains the gap?
options: The vectorised version trades at the close, holds fractions of shares and resizes on every bar
The vectorised version uses a different signal
The loop counts each gain twice
The vectorised version includes buy and hold
questions.explanation: Both use the same trend signal. The loop fills whole shares at the next open and resizes only on a signal change, so it trades differently from the column formula.
